instructions: Finely chop the onion and dice the 2 tomatoes. Mince the 2 garlic cloves.
Seed and thinly slice the jalapeño and put it in a small bowl for the table.
Crack the 8 eggs into a bowl, add 1/4 tsp of the salt and beat them with a fork until there are no streaks of white left.

Melt 2 tbsp ghee (or niter kibbeh, if you have it) in a large nonstick skillet over medium. Add the onion and cook for about 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's soft and starting to turn golden.
Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant. Stir in 1 tbsp tomato paste and the 1 tsp berbere and cook for 1 minute, stirring, until the paste turns a shade darker.
Add the tomatoes and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until the tomatoes soften and most of their juice has cooked off.
Turn the heat down to medium low and pour in the eggs. Leave them for about 20 seconds, then stir slowly with a spatula, pushing the set egg from the edges into the middle.
Keep stirring gently for 2 to 3 minutes. Take the pan off the heat while the eggs still look a little glossy. They keep cooking in the hot pan.
Chop a small handful of the cilantro and scatter it over the eggs. Taste them, and add a pinch more salt if they're flat.
Serve with injera or warm bread, with the sliced jalapeño on the side.
method_notes: Both read versions cook onion first, then scramble the eggs gently in the pan. SBS (Tinsae Elsdon's recipe, adapted by Adam Liaw) builds a base of red onion, garlic, fresh tomato and tomato paste before the eggs go in, stirs green chilli through at the end, finishes with coriander and serves it with a teff kita flatbread. Brundo scrambles the eggs in niter kibbeh and adds berbere or the hotter mitmita. This one cooks the berbere into the tomato base in ghee or niter kibbeh and puts the chilli on the side. No version had 20 or more ratings and RecipeTin Eats (the trusted cook for Ethiopian) has no version, so the first read version leads.
